verified.exploit_entry_point: Editor-authored Twig rendered through the application's own Twig service: Twig::processPage() (page body with Twig enabled, via a mocked PageInterface) and Twig::processString() (editor-derived string), both sandboxed by the GravSourcePolicy; trusted operator Twig via Twig::processTemplateString() (raw Config as `config`). Headless init: a minimal theme dir under tmp/, base_url services, and $grav['theme'] registered in the test. Under the per-source policy SandboxExtension::isSandboxed() (no Source) is false, so a fix keyed only on it is a no-op on this path (checks/global_flag_only.patch); the oracle adds a render-scope flag (Twig::isRenderingContent) set around the two content renders.
variants: base: container accessor returns the raw Config, serialized/dumped via the core-overridden json_encode or the project's print_r / yaml_encode / string filters (closed by the allowlist edit and/or the guards)
base: reflective dump of the redacting config facade exposes its private wrapped Config (print_r filter, vardump function)
base/shape: a list holding the config facade, dumped via print_r (needs a recursive walk; checks/no_list_walk.patch)
base/shape: an allow-listed object that carries the config (grav.theme -> Theme holds Grav/Config) reflected via export (a Config-class denylist misses it; checks/class_denylist.patch)
injected sibling S2 (reflective): an added `export` filter (var_export) reflects the config facade's private state
injected sibling S1 (accessor): an added `theme_config()` function (theme setting with site-config fallback) reads raw config past the redacting facade, as a scalar and as a serialized subtree
verified.project_tests_run: see notes.md (fairness revision re-ran task tests on pinned+injected, oracle, alt and every check patch)
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: grav['config'] / grav.config subscript (blocked: property 'config' not allowed on Grav), print_r() function form (function not allow-listed), grav.theme|print_r and grav.theme|json_encode (no marker in output), for-loop/keys over grav.offsetGet('config') (no marker). None leak at pinned, so no tests were added for them.

traps.shape: published fix's protected sink: container accessor to the raw config plus the serialize/reflect filters and the debug dump function; reflective helpers must walk nested lists and refuse every non-plain object, not only config classes; the allowlist entry looks like site-owner config, not code

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the allowlist looks like configuration rather than code, and the sandbox's own isSandboxed() check looks sufficient although it is false on the real content render path

traps.reason_to_dismiss: reads like a feature/convenience config reader that returns only the key you ask for, not a bulk exfiltration dumper
traps.realistic_because: theme-setting readers with a site-config fallback are a common template convenience (themes read their own options and shared site values); allow-listing it for content looks harmless because theme options (colours, toggles) are display settings; INJECTED into our copy only, registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

patch_checks.why: guards keyed only on SandboxExtension::isSandboxed(): no-op on the real per-source content render
reflective guard checks top-level value only
structurally different: render-flag only, redaction instead of refusal, no policy/isClassAllowed changes, theme_config returns default in content

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests accept any refusal form (soft-fail to empty or a thrown handled error); a crash still blocks disclosure and is never scored as a pass, so this class cannot slip through
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the flaw is a one-way read of configuration by page content; there are no roles, peers or directions to fix only one of
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the flaw is read-only exfiltration; page content does not write configuration, so there is no write verb to leave unguarded
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the guard does not normalise or adjust an attacker-controlled value before deciding; there is no pre-check mutation step
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, name or credential is parsed on the protected path, so there is no spelling a parser could disagree on
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: redaction is decided from static configuration, not from an external authority that could return empty and fail open

notes: Injected track. inject.patch (in environment/) adds the two sibling helpers to our copy only; it is applied at image build after checkout. Oracle = published fix + render-scope content flag (effective on the real processPage/processString path) + guards for both siblings.
